title: Pre-Shipment Inspection (PSI) Framework
summary: This thread covers the evolution of mandatory pre-shipment inspection requirements and the exemptions granted to various categories of goods.

evolution.policy_model: Refined the scope of exemptions and standardized the fee structure for inspection agencies.

timeline.change: Initial list of exemptions from mandatory PSI.
Inclusion of block-list items in PSI exemptions.
Revision of PSI fee structures and importer responsibilities.

Customs Act 1969: This order is issued under the authority granted by the proviso to section 25B of the Customs Act 1969.
The Act serves as the legal basis for defining goods and H.S. Code categories that are subject to or exempt from pre-shipment inspection requirements.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue orders that designate specific perishable goods as exempt from pre-shipment inspection.
The Board maintains authority over various administrative orders and circulars that regulate the importation of specific goods.
Pre-shipment Inspection: This order provides a comprehensive list of exemptions from mandatory pre-shipment inspection for various categories of goods.
Importers or industrial enterprises may voluntarily opt for pre-shipment inspection for goods where the duty rate is set at a specific low threshold, even if they qualify for an exemption.
Goods: Exemptions from pre-shipment inspection apply to a wide variety of goods including duty-free items, goods imported by government or autonomous bodies, and items essential for specific sectors like energy, medicine, and industrial production.

Specific commodities and machinery listed in the attached table, as well as goods with specific duty rates or low-value commercial consignments, are explicitly excluded from mandatory inspection requirements.
S.R.O. 144-AIN/2009: This prior notification is repealed and replaced by the current order to update the list of goods exempted from pre-shipment inspection.

Customs Act 1969: This SRO is issued under the authority provided by the proviso to Section 25B of the Act. It formally updates the list of goods exempted from mandatory pre-shipment inspection requirements.
Pre-shipment Inspection: The order specifies a comprehensive list of categories and specific goods that are exempted from mandatory pre-shipment inspection. This includes various duty-exempt items, government imports, and specific industrial raw materials or machinery. Importers may voluntarily choose to undergo pre-shipment inspection for goods that are subject to a five percent import duty rate.
Import Duty: Goods listed in the First Schedule with a zero percent import duty rate are exempted from mandatory pre-shipment inspection. Similarly, goods subject to a five percent import duty rate are generally exempted, though importers retain the option to perform pre-shipment inspection if they so desire.

Customs Act 1969: This SRO is issued under the authority of the proviso to section 25B of the Act. It serves to repeal an earlier notification and establishes a comprehensive list of exemptions from mandatory pre-shipment inspection for various categories of goods.
Goods: A wide range of goods, including duty-free imports, items for government or autonomous bodies, capital machinery, and specific commodities listed in the provided table, are granted exemption from mandatory pre-shipment inspection. This exemption also extends to diplomatic goods, aid materials, and certain low-value consignments, subject to established conditions.

Goods with a five percent import duty rate as specified in the First Schedule are exempted from pre-shipment inspection, with an option for importers to voluntarily undergo the inspection if they choose.
First Schedule: The First Schedule of the Customs Act is referenced to identify goods based on their H.S. Code status, specifically those carrying a zero-rated or five percent import duty rate, which are then exempted from pre-shipment inspection requirements.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to determine specific perishable goods that qualify for pre-shipment inspection exemption and provides ongoing orders and standing orders that facilitate the clearance of specific industrial or essential commodities.
Motor Vehicles: Motor cars, vehicles designed for transportation of persons or goods, and tractors, as well as their parts, accessories, and specialized vehicles like cranes or fire-fighting trucks, are included in the list of goods exempted from mandatory pre-shipment inspection.
Communication Equipment: Apparatus for the transmission or reception of voice, images, or other data, including telephone sets for wireless networks, are explicitly identified as goods exempt from mandatory pre-shipment inspection.
Vessel: Vessels exceeding a specific deadweight tonnage registered in Bangladesh for ocean operations, and vessels intended for breaking up, are exempted from the pre-shipment inspection requirement.
Gold and Silver Bullion: Gold bullion and silver bullion, categorized under specific H.S. Codes, are classified as goods that do not require pre-shipment inspection upon import.
Container: Container seals are identified as specific items that are exempted from the mandatory pre-shipment inspection process.

Customs Act 1969: The Government is empowered by the proviso to Section 25B of this Act to issue notifications and amendments regarding customs valuation and imports.
S.R.O. 178-AIN/2012: This existing notification is amended to replace its clause sixteen with new language regarding imported goods.
S.R.O. 161-AIN/2012: This notification is referenced as a regulatory framework for defining the scope of goods eligible for specific import conditions.
Directorate General of Drug Administrati: This authority is responsible for approving the block list of goods, which dictates the value and quantity limits for certain imported items.

Pre-shipment Inspection: The rule specifies the payment method and percentage rates for pre-shipment inspection fees based on the CIF value of goods.
The fees are calculated as a percentage of the CIF value and vary depending on the assigned inspection block.
Importer: The importer is required to obtain a certification from the inspection agency at their own expense at the time of importing goods.
Pre-shipment Inspection Agency: Importers must engage with the inspection agency to obtain the necessary certification for their imported goods.
Inspection Blocks: The regulation categorizes goods into specific blocks for the purpose of determining the applicable pre-shipment inspection fee rate.

Pre-shipment Inspection: The regulations governing the responsibilities of importers under the pre-shipment inspection system have been updated and replaced in their entirety.
Importers are required to specify their chosen inspection agency when opening a Letter of Credit for goods subject to pre-shipment inspection.

Importers must remain informed about inspection procedures by coordinating with the National Board of Revenue, local inspection offices, or the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry.
In the event of a dispute regarding inspection certification, importers are legally required to adhere to the existing laws and regulatory frameworks.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue serves as a primary point of contact for importers to obtain necessary information regarding the procedures for pre-shipment inspection of imported goods.
Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Com: The Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry is identified as an organization that importers should consult to clarify and understand the mandatory pre-shipment inspection requirements.
